import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def delete_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode

/-- Join two trees where every element of `l` is smaller than every element of `r`. -/
def mergeBST : BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty, r => r
  | BinarySearchTree.Node x ll lr, r =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node x ll (mergeBST lr r)

/-- Naive BST deletion. -/
def del (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => BinarySearchTree.Empty
  | BinarySearchTree.Node x l r =>
      if v < x then BinarySearchTree.Node x (del l v) r
      else if v > x then BinarySearchTree.Node x l (del r v)
      else mergeBST l r

-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def delete (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : delete_precond t v) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  del t v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def delete_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : delete_precond t v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t \ {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma

theorem view_mergeBST (l r : BinarySearchTree) :
    view (mergeBST l r) = view l ∪ view r := by
  induction l with
  | Empty => simp [mergeBST, view]
  | Node x ll lr _ ihr =>
      ext z
      simp only [mergeBST, view, ihr, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      tauto

theorem is_bst_mergeBST (l r : BinarySearchTree) (hl : is_bst l) (hr : is_bst r)
    (hsep : ∀ a ∈ view l, ∀ b ∈ view r, a < b) : is_bst (mergeBST l r) := by
  induction l with
  | Empty => simpa [mergeBST] using hr
  | Node x ll lr ihl ihr =>
      simp only [is_bst] at hl
      obtain ⟨hlt, hll, hgt, hlr⟩ := hl
      have hx : x ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x ll lr) := by
        simp [view]
      refine ⟨hlt, hll, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro z hz
        rw [view_mergeBST] at hz
        rcases hz with hz | hz
        · exact hgt z hz
        · exact hsep x hx z hz
      · refine ihr hlr ?_
        intro a ha b hb
        refine hsep a ?_ b hb
        simp [view, ha]

theorem del_correct : ∀ (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int), is_bst t →
    is_bst (del t v) ∧ view (del t v) = view t \ {v} := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | Empty => intro v _; exact ⟨trivial, by simp [del, view]⟩
  | Node x l r ihl ihr =>
      intro v h
      simp only [is_bst] at h
      obtain ⟨hlt, hl, hgt, hr⟩ := h
      by_cases h1 : v < x
      · obtain ⟨ihl1, ihl2⟩ := ihl v hl
        simp only [del, if_pos h1]
        refine ⟨⟨?_, ihl1, hgt, hr⟩, ?_⟩
        · intro z hz
          rw [ihl2] at hz
          exact hlt z hz.1
        · ext z
          simp only [view, ihl2, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_diff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          constructor
          · rintro ((⟨hz, hzv⟩ | hz) | hz)
            · exact ⟨Or.inl (Or.inl hz), hzv⟩
            · refine ⟨Or.inl (Or.inr hz), ?_⟩
              have := hgt z hz
              omega
            · subst hz
              exact ⟨Or.inr rfl, by omega⟩
          · rintro ⟨(hz | hz) | hz, hzv⟩
            · exact Or.inl (Or.inl ⟨hz, hzv⟩)
            · exact Or.inl (Or.inr hz)
            · exact Or.inr hz
      · by_cases h2 : v > x
        · obtain ⟨ihr1, ihr2⟩ := ihr v hr
          simp only [del, if_neg h1, if_pos h2]
          refine ⟨⟨hlt, hl, ?_, ihr1⟩, ?_⟩
          · intro z hz
            rw [ihr2] at hz
            exact hgt z hz.1
          · ext z
            simp only [view, ihr2, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_diff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
            constructor
            · rintro ((hz | ⟨hz, hzv⟩) | hz)
              · refine ⟨Or.inl (Or.inl hz), ?_⟩
                have := hlt z hz
                omega
              · exact ⟨Or.inl (Or.inr hz), hzv⟩
              · subst hz
                exact ⟨Or.inr rfl, by omega⟩
            · rintro ⟨(hz | hz) | hz, hzv⟩
              · exact Or.inl (Or.inl hz)
              · exact Or.inl (Or.inr ⟨hz, hzv⟩)
              · exact Or.inr hz
        · have hvx : v = x := by omega
          subst hvx
          simp only [del, if_neg h1]
          constructor
          · refine is_bst_mergeBST l r hl hr ?_
            intro a ha b hb
            have := hlt a ha
            have := hgt b hb
            omega
          · ext z
            simp only [view_mergeBST, view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_diff,
              Set.mem_singleton_iff]
            constructor
            · rintro (hz | hz)
              · refine ⟨Or.inl (Or.inl hz), ?_⟩
                have := hlt z hz
                omega
              · refine ⟨Or.inl (Or.inr hz), ?_⟩
                have := hgt z hz
                omega
            · rintro ⟨(hz | hz) | hz, hzv⟩
              · exact Or.inl hz
              · exact Or.inr hz
              · exact absurd hz hzv

-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem delete_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : delete_precond t v) :
    delete_postcond t v (delete t v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  simpa [delete] using del_correct t v h_precond
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`LEAN VERIFIED` — only warnings remain, both from the unchanged skeleton (`delete_precond`'s unused `v`, and the unused `h_precond` in `delete`).

## What I did

I edited only the four marker regions in `Solution.lean`.

**auxcode** — two definitions:
- `mergeBST l r`: joins two trees when everything in `l` is below everything in `r`. It recurses structurally on the *left* tree (`Node x ll lr, r ↦ Node x ll (mergeBST lr r)`) rather than hoisting the minimum out of `r`. Same observable behavior as the textbook "replace with successor" join, but the recursion is structural and the invariant argument is one step.
- `del t v`: the naive delete — descend left/right on comparison, and at the matching node return `mergeBST l r`.

**code** — `delete t v _ := del t v` (the precondition isn't needed to *define* the result, only to prove it correct).

**lemma** — three results:
- `view_mergeBST : view (mergeBST l r) = view l ∪ view r`.
- `is_bst_mergeBST`: BST-ness is preserved given `is_bst l`, `is_bst r`, and separation `∀ a ∈ view l, ∀ b ∈ view r, a < b`. The new root `x` dominates `mergeBST lr r` because `view lr > x` from the left tree's invariant and `view r > x` from separation.
- `del_correct`: by induction on `t`, both postconditions at once. The set equations need the BST invariant to know `v` can't hide in the untouched subtree (e.g. when `v < x`, every element of `r` exceeds `x > v`), and in the deletion case that `x ∉ view l ∪ view r`.

**proof** — `simpa [delete] using del_correct t v h_precond`.

No `sorry`, `axiom`, `partial`, `unsafe`, or `@[extern]`/`@[implemented_by]`; `del` and `mergeBST` are structurally recursive, so no termination escape hatch was used either. I did burn one of the 15 compiler checks re-running `./check.sh` before applying the fixes from the first run's output — it returned identical errors, so checks 1 and 2 are the same result.
